subject: Recap & next steps — token volumes, pricing, batching
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Jonathan Li <jonathan.li@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Mar 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Recap & next steps — token volumes, pricing, batching

Hi Jonathan — thanks again for the productive call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned:

1) Usage profile (your confirmation needed)
- Estimated steady-state: ~200M tokens/month total (breakdown: ~50M prompts, ~150M completions)
- Typical request: short prompt + medium completion (average ~200 tokens per request)
- Traffic shape: steady throughout the day with predictable peaks during weekday events

2) Budget target and unit economics
- You mentioned a target spend of roughly $2k–$3k/month. That implies a target of ~$10–$15 per 1M tokens.
- For context, our hosted API list pricing for this model is $10/1M tokens (prompt+completion billed together). Dedicated/reserved capacity commitments can bring unit cost down (we’ve seen effective $7–$8/1M at commit levels similar to your volume).

3) Batching & concurrency assumptions
- Important for cost: continuous batching (steady stream of small requests) usually yields better packing into GPU batches and reduces per-token compute cost by ~15–30% vs naive single-request throughput.
- From the call I heard: average concurrency ~60–100, with short requests. Please confirm expected peak RPS and burst tolerance — that will determine whether you should go hosted vs reserved.

4) Next steps
- Jonathan: confirm the monthly token split and peak RPS/burst windows.
- Camila/Marissa: I’ll put together a proposed pricing PDF (hosted vs dedicated scenarios + assumed batching uplift) and sample SLA language for Reserved capacity.
- Optional: 30-day trial on a small reserved pool so you can validate latency and batching benefits against your workload.

Attachments: I’ll attach a draft pricing summary and our SOC2 snapshot for procurement to review.

Thanks — Camila
Camila Reyes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
camila@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Recap & next steps — token volumes, pricing, batching

Camila — thanks for the summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Volumes: the 200M tokens/month is a good midpoint for our FY26 planning. We expect a fairly even distribution with occasional daily peaks during reporting windows.
- Concurrency: steady-state concurrency is ~80 active requests on average, peaks up to ~250 RPS for ~15 minute windows during events. We could tolerate some tail latency during peaks but prefer to avoid queueing.
- Budget: our procurement guidance is $2k–$3k/mo to start; if unit economics are strong we can expand in Q3.

Two asks: can you show modeled unit cost at 200M tokens for both hosted and a 12-month reserved commitment? Also please call out assumptions about batching impact on latency — continuous batching sounds great for cost but we need to understand 95th percentile latency.

I’ll loop procurement if we need to get legal/PO involved. Thanks — J

From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Jonathan Li <jonathan.li@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 31 Mar 2026 08:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps — token volumes, pricing, batching

Thanks Jonathan — answering inline and adding assumptions so procurement has clear numbers.

Modeled options (assumes 200M tokens/month):
- Hosted (no commit): $10 / 1M tokens => $2,000 / month.
- Dedicated (12-month reserve, moderate commit): effective $7 / 1M tokens => $1,400 / month (requires monthly reserved baseline; includes burst at higher per-token increments).

Batching & latency assumptions:
- Continuous batching benefit depends on request size distribution and concurrency. For your profile (many small-to-medium requests, steady flow): we model a ~20% reduction in per-token compute cost vs single-request baseline. That already informs the hosted estimate above (we conservatively priced hosted without additional uplift).
- Latency: with continuous batching and avg concurrency ~80 we expect median latencies similar to hosted baseline (~50–120ms per token depending on model and IO), and 95th percentile can rise during packing to ~600–900ms for full responses in worst-case short-request packing scenarios. Dedicated reserved pools with configured max-batch-window tuning can limit 95th percentile tail while preserving batching gains.

Key assumptions we used in the model (please confirm if these are wrong):
- Average request size: 50 prompt tokens + 150 completion tokens (200 tokens total).
- Average tokens per month: 200M.
- Steady concurrency target: 60–100, peaks to 250 RPS for short windows.
- Continuous traffic (no extreme bursty spikes >2x baseline for >5 minutes).

Deliverables I’ll send by end of day:
- proposed_pricing_v1.pdf (hosted vs dedicated scenarios, monthly math, sensitivity to batching uplift)
- SOC2 summary (SOC2-cert-summary.pdf) for procurement
- Short runbook describing recommended batch_window settings and concurrency guardrails for your SREs

If procurement is happy with the pricing, we can spin up a 30-day evaluation on a small reserved pool (same model) so you can run real traffic and we’ll instrument token/cost dashboards.

Looping Marissa and Aditya to help with any technical follow-up and to schedule the eval onboarding.

— Camila

Attachment stubs: proposed_pricing_v1.pdf (1 page summary), SOC2-cert-summary.pdf
